about: MUTATING — retire ONE ServiceAccount, Role or RoleBinding the tree no longer declares (infra/forge/retire-access-object.sh <kind> <namespace> <name> <plan_sha256>; backlog 526bedf2). delete-orphan-object withholds these kinds from its kind floor on purpose — a ServiceAccount's deletion invalidates the tokens issued from it, and a privilege's deletion can remove a live capability nobody wrote down — so an undeclared one was retired by hand with the admin kubeconfig; David 2026-10-18: manually running any ops command is a gap in BOSS coverage. This verb is retire-volume-claim's sibling for privileges and does NOT widen delete-orphan-object's floor, which stays Service, ConfigMap, Deployment, CronJob, Job: these three kinds become deletable only under a passkey. AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY, design 17835005: the read-only plan-an-access-object-retirement renders bytes onto the approve step, an allowed passkey signs them, and the runner hands this write sha256 of the SIGNED plan. THE AUTHORITY IS DERIVED: the script re-renders at call time and acts only when the plan still hashes to the approved value — the kind is ServiceAccount, Role or RoleBinding and nothing else; the name is not protected (ServiceAccount default, anything named break-glass*, in any namespace); the manifest directories are clean in git; undeclared-objects.sh --check names it undeclared (refusing an unowned namespace, a declared object, an exempt or controller-owned one, and one not live); it is not being deleted and has no owner; and NOTHING CONSUMES IT, every list read failing closed: for a ServiceAccount, no Pod in any phase runs as it and no Job, CronJob, Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet or ReplicaSet would (the holders of its issued tokens), no Secret is a long-lived token issued from it, and no RoleBinding in any namespace nor ClusterRoleBinding grants it; for a Role, no RoleBinding grants it; for a RoleBinding, every subject is a ServiceAccount (a User or Group is refused: no read names its holders) and none runs a Pod or would. Any drift refuses (exit 78) naming both hashes; the kind is in the plan, so a plan signed for one kind never deletes another; and a second run of an applied plan finds the object gone and refuses, so one approval deletes at most once. CAPTURE BEFORE DELETE, ON THE RECORD: the object's YAML is attached to this ops-request through boss attach, which reads the bytes back; only a verified attachment lets the delete run. THE WRITE is one DELETE carrying DeleteOptions.preconditions.uid. THE EFFECT: the object read back gone — the server's NotFound, or its name held by another uid — and nothing else counts: a get that answers Forbidden, times out, or returns no document or no uid is deleted-not-proven-gone, exit 1. Initial refusals exit 78 without writes. Timeout 300 covers the derivation's parse, the attach, and a 60 s read-back.
effect: ^retire-access-object: (ServiceAccount|Role|RoleBinding) [a-z0-9-]+/[a-z0-9.-]+ uid [0-9a-f-]{36} is gone \(read back: (NotFound|its name is now held by uid [0-9a-f-]+, a different object)\)$
